attributes.residual: 18 raw differing words at 141/141, and every one is now named. (1) ONE live-zero word at +0x118: ours `li r25,0` (3b200000), target `addi r25,r26,0` (3b3a0000) copying the x=0 that `li r26,0` just seeded - the shipped LIVE-ZERO VALUE class (equivalent_zero_form, proof zero_value_dataflow) is the exact shape, with declared_zero_register 26. (2) ONE 2-atom transposition at +0x148/+0x14c: `addi r6,r6,156` and `li r5,2` are exchanged, both independent, no relocation. (3) ONE further 2-atom transposition at +0x74/+0x78: ours forms lbl_80240FA0 before lbl_80240FB0, the target the other way round - this window DOES carry two ADDR16_LO relocations naming different symbols, so it needs verify_relocation_binding. (4) The remaining ~14 words are a volatile-register recolor across the pad-latch loop (our @0x70 addi r8 / @0x74 addi r5 / @0x78 addi r7 / @0x88 add r6 / @0x8c add r9 against the target's @0x70 addi r9 / @0x74 addi r8 / @0x78 addi r5 / @0x88 add r7 / @0x8c add r6) and the two entry-row address computations. A postprocessor close would therefore be a FOUR-stage composed rule (two permutations + copy_register_fields + equivalent_zero_form); it has not been derived and the recolor half's consistency has not been proved.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: One probe: name the two table bases as locals in source order (`u32* t1 = lbl_80240FB0; u32* t2 = lbl_80240FA0;`) before the loop and index them. If the +0x74/+0x78 pair does not swap, the address-materialisation order is scheduler-owned rather than source-owned and the four-stage composed rule is the only remaining path.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- `fnasm game/pb/pb_diag pbDiagDrawMenu 0x5c:0xb0 --diff` at the committed state shows the three `lis` in identical order in both streams and only the three `addi` ADDR16_LO words permuted, which is what makes a source-side reorder plausible; the probe itself has NOT been compiled. Definition sites for the registers this window writes, quoted from `fnasm game/pb/pb_diag pbDiagDrawMenu 0x5c:0xb0` on OUR stream: @0x70 `addi r8,r5,0 @lbl_80240FC0(ADDR16_LO)`, @0x74 `addi r5,r3,0 @lbl_80240FA0(ADDR16_LO)`, @0x78 `addi r7,r4,0 @lbl_80240FB0(ADDR16_LO)`, @0x88 `add r6,r7,r3`, @0x8c `add r9,r30,r3`; the target's counterparts are @0x70 `addi r9,r5,0 @lbl_80240FC0`, @0x74 `addi r8,r4,0 @lbl_80240FB0`, @0x78 `addi r5,r3,0 @lbl_80240FA0`, @0x88 `add r7,r8,r3`, @0x8c `add r6,r30,r3`. Each register named above is written exactly once inside this window in its own stream.
hypothesis.statement: The +0x74/+0x78 relocation-carrying transposition is the ROOT of the volatile recolor, not a peer of it: the three table addresses are formed in source order lbl_80240FC0, lbl_80240FB0, lbl_80240FA0 (lines 1744-1746) and the target emits the three ADDR16_LO `addi`s in exactly that order, while ours emits FC0, FA0, FB0 - so a source form that forces the FB0 address to be materialised before the FA0 one (for example splitting the loop body's three assignments so the tbl1 store's base is named as a local before the tbl2 store's) should re-order the two `addi`s and may collapse the whole scratch-register cascade in that loop with them, leaving only the single live-zero word.
